chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
title: Jo Jones replaces Shadow Wilson
summary: Basie's drummer joins the Jacquet band and his experience and stories make working with him a lesson.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: In the same band, we had... Shadow Wilson left some time during that summer, I believe. Shadow was another guy who had a kind of restless nature. When Shadow left, we got Jo Jones

of the Count Basie Band, of Count Basie fame rather. A lot of people refer to him as "Old Man Jo Jones" and all sorts of things, because of the fact that there are two very good drummers who bear the same name as Jo Jones. One of them is in Philadelphia, the drummer who everybody calls Philly Joe Jones. Well, this was the Jo Jones of the Count Basie fame, the older man, and he's had a lot to do with the drumming situation -- as far as a turning point in drumming.

But working with him was an experience in another way, because of his mature knowledge, and he was an older person than the other musicians, and there are things that he would say just from his knowhow, and some of the stories that he'd tell... And I've always been a good listener. And working with him was a real experience.
